main_text.l: V. Nisi forte quia vasis argenteis nō vtimur sem
per, iccirco fordibus que sunt confpurcata vitra plá
cent: aut illuuie immundæ propterea gratæ sunt mu-
lieres, q splendido vestitu quotidie non fefe ornant.
V I. In illa igitur amabo te, curā incūbe, vtLatinas
postbac et Ciceronianas magis abs te literas accipiā.
V II. Nofti domū ad parentes, præceptores, me-
cœnates missas literas testimonia quædam diligentiæ
& profectus in studijs effe.
VIII. Magnam ego meo testimonio tui expecta-
tionem apud parentes & quosdam ordinis senatorij
viros concitaui.
IX. Fac ergo bi vt intelligant, veritatis non gra
tiæ meum istud testimonium extitisse.
X. Ita gratū abunde erga me te declarabis: et quā
collectā bonorū doctorumq; virorū iam gratiam ha
bes, non effundes, sed retinebis: honestū etiam domū
aliquādo reuersus, in patria locū confequi poteris.
Quemadmodū verò in laudationibus
exēpla conati sumus exercitij gratia pro-
ponere laudis personarū, rerum, factorum
& dictorū:ita quoq; in iisdem vt reprehen
sio fit atq; vituperatio instituēda, breuiter
ostendemus. Et quidem ad personarū re-
prehēsiones quod attinet, argumētis illæ
fiūt quinque potissimūm ex locis desum
ptis. Primò caufarū: causa enim absoluta
turpitudinis atq; dedecoris est vitium.

page.notes: Printed text is set in long s (s) throughout the page; I have transcribed it as plain s per the rules. Doubtful readings: "studijs" and "reuersus" are clear enough, but the word after "abunde" in X ("erga") and the "ī" in "gratū" are as printed. The first line of V has a broken hyphen "mu- lieres" which is kept. The fragment "vtLatinas" in VI is printed as one word and kept as such. Last paragraph line 1 partially cut at the top right of the scan; the reading "Quemadmodū verò" is clear. Scan edge shows a dark gutter at the right side; no text lost there.
